symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of cells holding an input, that is, the length of the input string.
symbols.quote: The running time cost of a machine is the number of steps it takes on an input, written as a function of the input length $n$, the number of cells that hold the input, and taken in the worst case over all inputs of that length.

symbols.name: machine
symbols.meaning: The single machine whose running time the main theorem bounds.
symbols.quote: it gives one machine $A$ that multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly.

symbols.name: fixed exponent constant
symbols.meaning: A fixed constant, equal to $2^{-182}$, that sets the exponent $1-\kappa$ in the running time bound.
symbols.quote: The bound on its running time has the form $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, where $\kappa = 2^{-182}$ is a fixed constant.

symbols.name: running time cost
symbols.meaning: The running time cost of machine A as a function of the input length n: the largest number of steps A takes on any input of that length.
symbols.quote: For a machine $A$ and an input length $n$, the running time cost is $T_A(n)$, the largest number of steps $A$ takes on any input of length $n$.

symbols.name: scanning machine
symbols.meaning: The example machine that reads cells from left to right and halts at the first cell holding 1 or at the last cell.
symbols.quote: Take the machine $M$ that starts on the first cell.
